notes: SHIP v1.14.381 - DESKTOP TOOLS WIRED TO THE 768 ART. Owner: 768 dashboard is the target, wire desktop tools. This closes the D7/R4 deferral that .378 shipped around, and it does NOT need the desktop strip recut web-Claude was going to cut as ART-DROP-380. THE DEFERRAL AND WHY IT DISSOLVED: .378 scoped the art-first card face to max-width 639.98px because the assets are 1:1 and the desktop card ran roughly 2:1, and ART-DROP-SHIP-379 R4 explicitly forbade shipping a stopgap desktop cover-crop. The unstated assumption was that the CARD aspect is fixed and the ART must be recut to match it. With the owner ruling that the 768 dashboard set IS the target generation, the cheaper and better answer is the reverse: give the desktop card the same aspect-ratio:1/1 the art already has. Result is zero crop at every width, and it makes TOOLS consistent with the OPS wall, which has been aspect-ratio:1/1 on every shell all along - that was the O4 finding from the .377 OBSERVE pass. No new art is required and no strip set needs cutting; tell web-Claude ART-DROP-380 is unnecessary for both surfaces. THE CHANGE IS SMALL: the four .rf-art rules were lifted out of their @media (max-width:639.98px) wrapper so they now apply at every shell. Nothing else about the face changed - D5's scrim gradient, the bottom-left annotation, the one-line ellipsised subtitle, the per-card --rfac accent, corner brackets, :active press and the scan-sweep animation are all exactly as shipped in .378. Still scoped to #ref-grid, so #work-grid and .deploy-tools-grid, which share the .rf-card class, remain untouched. SECOND HALF, AND THIS SHIP CREATED THE NEED FOR IT: with the face applying at all widths, .rf-cic is display:none everywhere, so the seven elements on those cards were downloading on every load and rendering nowhere. Per the drop's A4 they are COMMENTED OUT with an ART-376 fallback marker rather than deleted, so a revert restores them intact. That left seven rasters - phantom-ref-cli/compass/ghostecho/hardware/hwref/know-256.webp and phantom-ref-optics-384.webp - with ZERO live references anywhere, verified by stripping HTML comments before counting rather than by eye, while still sitting in PRECACHE_URLS. That is exactly the dead weight the .364 cleanup purged, and this ship made it dead, so this ship cleans it: seven precache entries removed, 61 back down to 54. The FILES stay on disk per the orphan-but-retained precedent, so the fallback comments can be uncommented without re-adding assets. Every remaining precache path verified to exist. NOT TOUCHED: the nine live rf-i-img consumers in #work-grid and .deploy-tools-grid - those are a separate unmigrated surface flagged in the SHIP-ART-PARITY-SWEEP Phase 1 report and NOT traced yet - the OPS wall, the NAV v2 glyphs, the BUILD banners, all art from .377/.378, the legacy house, and ?legacy=1. DEVICE-VERIFY, and the desktop half is the point of this ship: (1) badge reads v1.14.381. (2) LAPTOP OR LANDSCAPE - the seven TOOLS cards must now show the SAME art-first face as the phone: full-bleed art, no icon-in-a-box, label bottom-left over the scrim. This is the change. (3) NO CROP - the art is square and the card is now square, so nothing should be cut off at any width. Drag the window across 640px and 980px; the grid goes 2 to 3 to 4 columns and the cards should stay square throughout, just larger. (4) LEGIBILITY at the larger desktop size - the type was tuned for a ~172px phone card and desktop cards are ~232 to 243px, so the label may read SMALL. If it does, that is a type-scale tune, not a revert; report it and I will add a desktop step. (5) Phone must be UNCHANGED from .378. (6) OFFLINE PASS - seven precache entries were removed, so relaunch online once then airplane-mode and reopen; all seven card arts must still render from cache. (7) ?legacy=1 unchanged. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - restores the phone-only media query, uncomments the seven img elements and restores their seven precache entries together.
